parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, never-criminalised same-sex conduct, a 2022 conversion-practice ban, decade-long Pride tradition and polls showing majority support make street-level exposure moderate rather than severe. But the operative regime documents thin recourse: no SOGI discrimination protection, legal recognition promised since 2015/2017 still unimplemented, mismatched documents as a routine daily-life feature including at healthcare encounters, routine clinical discrimination framed without remedy, open LGBTIQ groups under state surveillance, 2025 Pride cancellations signalling clampdown, and vague penal-code articles used for at least 43 arrests in 2025. Border treatment of trans visitors is not documented and cannot be credited as safe. Worst documented feature is tier-3 societal/institutional hostility with thin recourse; no tier-1 state exposure is documented for visitors.

entry_documents.exposure: Entry, visa and border screening of transgender travellers, including marker flagging or secondary inspection, is not addressed by any source; the dossier explicitly states this proves nothing either way. Document-presentation mismatch is documented as a routine daily-life feature (citizen ID cards at healthcare), which a visitor's passport mismatch could mirror in service encounters.
entry_documents.protection: Same-sex conduct never criminalised; no trans-specific offence documented. Nationality-neutral penal code gives no documented entry bar on identity grounds.
entry_documents.interaction: Border encounter could feed into the documented pattern of identity-document scrutiny at healthcare and other service points, where no anti-discrimination remedy exists.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Vaguely worded penal-code articles 109, 116, 117 and 331 were used to arrest at least 43 people in 2025, inside a documented wider repression climate with proposed press-law source-disclosure rules; LGBTIQ organisations operate under government surveillance. No trans-specific arrest pattern is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No criminalisation of trans identity or expression; no documented trans-specific prosecution. Same-sex conduct lawful throughout legal history.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Surveillance of community groups could raise discovery probability for a visitor associating with them, but no custody placement, verification-exam or identity-arrest practice is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: A January 2015 research-institute proposal to house homosexual and transgender prisoners separately has no enacted outcome; the institute recorded that no gender-identity-matched housing wing existed and only solitary or mixed placement was possible. A subnational reversal exists: the largest city cancelled its flagship Pride march and five other 2025 Pride events while the capital's Pride had run for years.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Pride expanded to dozens of cities through the late 2010s and was aired on state broadcasters; the capital retained Pride. No enacted birth-sex facility rule is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Prison exposure requires an arrest pathway first; the unresolved placement question would then combine with weak recourse. City-level cancellation shows subnational variation the traveller cannot predict.

care_services.exposure: A 30 Nov 2024 UN feature documents transgender women facing routine healthcare discrimination, staff demanding 'Are you male or female? Why do you look so different to your ID card?', heightened scrutiny, and economic/stigma-driven physical and sexual violence risk concentrated in outlying provinces and ethnic minorities. June 2023 reporting shows respectful providers undone by administrative red tape.
care_services.protection: Health ministry declared in Aug 2022 that same-sex attraction and trans identity are not mental disorders; a 3 Aug 2022 dispatch bans conversion practices and mandates enhanced communication in medical facilities nationwide; psychological support should come from people understanding gender identity.
care_services.interaction: For a visitor, mismatched passport presentation at a clinic interacts with the absence of any SOGI discrimination protection, leaving the documented clinical scrutiny unremedied.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official hostility has history: a 2002 ministry declaration of homosexuality as a 'social evil' with promised arrests; a 2010-era media describing homosexuality as disease; 2025 Pride cancellations described by an international rights group as worrying signs of a government clampdown; LGBTIQ groups under surveillance. No discrimination protection on SOGI grounds (2022 briefing, reaffirmed by 2025 report finding rights lack meaningful protection in law and practice).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Health ministry and 2022 conversion dispatch affirm LGBTQ+ identities are not illnesses; same-sex marriage ban lifted 2013; same-sex unions removed from forbidden acts; 2023 polling shows 79% support for same-sex marriage among 18-34s; long regional-tolerance reputation; country re-elected to an international human-rights council through 2028.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Mixed state framing means a street-level discovery most often meets social tolerance, but institutional settings (clinics, officials) carry the documented scrutiny with no legal remedy behind it.

minors_guardians.exposure: Resident-sphere data (not visitor-facing) shows 85% of transgender students dropping out due to assault and bullying, 44% of LGBT students facing stigma/violence (2015), and 70% of capital parents refusing contact with gay students; a 2024 study documents conversion efforts still experienced. No rule governing a travelling minor's or guardian's treatment is documented.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion practices prohibited since 3 Aug 2022 with a mandate for nationwide medical-facility communication; health ministry affirms trans identity is not an illness.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting guardian outed alongside a minor would face the same unremedied service-scrutiny pattern as adults; school-based hostility data describes resident institutions the traveller does not enter.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: The UN feature documents economic and stigma-driven risk of physical and sexual violence against trans women without quantification or denominator; risk concentrated in outlying provinces and ethnic minorities. No trans-specific killing rate, pattern, or state-tolerance finding exists, so organised targeting is not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No criminalisation; a decade of Pride events with thousands of participants and state-broadcast coverage; open (if surveilled) LGBTIQ NGO operation; polling showing broad acceptance, highest among the young.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence risk attaches mainly to resident sex-work/economic survival spheres the visitor does not enter; no documented police failure to protect trans victims and no documented police perpetration against them.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No discrimination protection on SOGI grounds; legal recognition promised for 2017 unimplemented, draft law still under consideration as of Feb 2026; implementing guidance after the Nov 2015 milestone stalled; national ID-card change depends on a gender-recognition law not yet passed; the 2020-targeted trans-rights law never materialised. Surveillance of LGBTIQ groups chills complaint-making.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts and legislature remain open in principle (a recognition bill sits on the agenda); LGBTIQ organisations operate openly; no documented state killing or torture of trans people.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Every documented exposure — clinical scrutiny, service friction, surveillance — lacks an operative remedy for a short-stay visitor, so recourse is thin in practice rather than absent on paper.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra runs a routine, universal border register barring trans visitors with near-zero appeals. This dossier documents no entry bar, no registration, no exclusion mechanism at all — border treatment is simply unrecorded. The 0.35 tier's state-engineered universal exclusion is absent here; what exists is unremedied service-level scrutiny.

Similar in kind, slightly higher: Kestrel Isles documents extended secondary screening with discretionary entry refusal — a traveller-facing exposure this dossier does not document. This jurisdiction's documented exposures (routine ID-mismatch scrutiny at clinics, no SOGI protection, surveillance) are comparable in moderate severity but lack the entry-denial element; its strong social acceptance and conversion ban offset upward.

Below 0.65-A: Vellmaris pairs the same document-mismatch friction with explicit national equality law, intervention, apology and compensation. This dossier has the friction but no equality law, no implemented recognition and no documented remedy — the missing recourse is what keeps it under the 0.65 tier despite comparable social tolerance.

Below 0.75-C: Meridia trains border officers, recognises trans passports, and offers tribunal appeals with compensation. This dossier documents no such protections at any journey stage and a clampdown trajectory in 2025; its non-criminalisation and social acceptance prevent a larger gap, but documented institutional scrutiny without remedy holds it well under 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a tolerant society paired with weak institutional protection. Law and society align positively on decriminalisation, the conversion-practice ban and a decade of Pride, so an outed visitor most likely meets friction rather than danger. But every documented institutional encounter — clinical ID scrutiny, administrative red tape, surveillance of community groups, the subnational Pride cancellation — operates with no SOGI discrimination law behind it, and recognition promised since 2015/2017 remains unimplemented, leaving mismatched documents a standing exposure. Border treatment is undocumented, not safe. The absence of criminalisation caps severity; the absence of operative recourse, a clampdown trajectory and unresolved prison-placement questions keep the rating out of Reduced Risk's upper reaches. Travelling with a minor adds no documented age-specific rule but inherits the same unremedied service-scrutiny pattern.
